question: Why is supreme Brahman called the inner self and emission?
premises: Supreme imperishable Brahman's own nature is called the inner self.
Emission, named action, causes the birth of beings' states.
Because of greatness and expansion, Brahman is denoted by the inner-self word.
Consciousness-being has unceasing dharma as its nature.
Brahman's consciousness-nature is unlimited externally and embraces world-power through sovereign freedom.
Emission manifests external being and inner-external being.
Emission gradually causes the birth of beings from Brahma-knowers to inert beings, manifesting inert and non-inert variety.
Emission also makes the birth of truth when the false world of being is dissolved.
inference: Supreme Brahman is called the inner self and emission because its unbounded consciousness-power manifests all beings, states, and truths.

plain_english: The blessed Lord said: the supreme imperishable Brahman, whose own nature is called the inner self, is emission named action, causing the birth of beings' states; because of its greatness and expansion it is denoted by the word inner self; consciousness-being, whose nature is unceasing dharma, is Brahman unlimited externally, and through sovereign freedom embracing world-power it manifests external and inner-external being; that emission gradually causes the birth of beings from Brahma-knowers to inert things, manifesting inert and non-inert variety, and also makes the birth of truth when the false world of being is dissolved.
